elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l02.intro
elements.html:
Distinguish explicit rules, learning from examples, and generative output without treating them as mutually exclusive eras.

Some software follows rules people specify. Machine learning fits patterns using data. Generative AI produces content such as text or images. These approaches coexist: a generative model can be machine learning, and a product can combine models with ordinary rules. Training adjusts a model using data; inference uses the trained model. A useful test asks how a system works, not just whether its label says AI.

Practice scenario

Three fictional tools: A sends a reminder when a timer reaches zero. B learns to label plant photos from labeled examples. C generates a new club announcement from a brief.

choices.text: A is obsolete; B and C replaced all rules.
A uses an explicit rule; B learns from examples; C generates content and may also use machine learning.
All three must be conscious to work.

elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l02.approaches.feedback.eras
elements.html: Rules still run timers, checks and many parts of AI applications.

elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l02.approaches.feedback.mix
elements.html: These categories overlap rather than forming a simple replacement timeline.

elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l02.approaches.feedback.all
elements.html: None of these behaviors establishes consciousness.

elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l02.inference
elements.title: A trained plant model labels one new photo. What is this step?

choices.text: Training must happen again for every photo.
Inference: applying the trained model to a new input.
Proof that its label is correct.

elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l02.inference.feedback.train
elements.html: Using a trained model does not by itself imply its parameters changed.

elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l02.inference.feedback.infer
elements.html: Right. Separate using the model from changing it during training.

elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l02.inference.feedback.certain
elements.html: A prediction still needs evaluation.

elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l02.overlap_check
elements.title: Can a generative system also use machine learning?

choices.text: No; they must be separate technologies.

elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l02.overlap_check.feedback.yes
elements.html: Generation describes output, while learning describes how patterns are fitted.

elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l02.overlap_check.feedback.no
elements.html: A generative model can learn from data.

elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l02.transfer
elements.title: Invent a simple rule-based tool and a tool that learns from examples. Explain how you would test the second on examples it did not train on.
elements.description: Practice text only. Saved on this device. Reviewed by you or an educator, not AI graded.

validators.text: Add enough reasoning to review (at least 30 characters).

elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l02.rubric
elements.html:
Self-check

  • Rule example has an explicit condition/action.
  • Learning example uses data to fit patterns.
  • Test includes new examples and a way to identify errors.

Systems can combine approaches. Do not date a single clean switch from rules to learning or infer consciousness from outputs.
